title: Constraint-Aware Coding-Sequence Design for Nicotiana benthamiana: A 49,257-Record Benchmark and Codon-Reference Sensitivity Analysis
content: Synonymous coding DNA sequence (CDS) design for plant expression constructs must balance host codon adaptation against guanine-cytosine (GC) composition, restriction-site avoidance, and sequence-integrity constraints, yet benchmark outcomes can depend strongly on the chosen codon-usage reference. Using FactorForge v3.2.0, an open-source CDS design and sequence-review workflow, we evaluated four rule-based design presets (Balanced, High-CAI, GC-target, and Assembly-friendly) on 49,257 reference-derived Nicotiana benthamiana CDS/protein records from the Sol Genomics Network (SGN) QLD183 resource (seed 320), scoring sequence integrity, a historical 55-65% GC window, and absence of BsaI/BpiI/BsmBI sites. With the legacy packaged codon reference, Assembly-friendly passed all three criteria for 63.37% of records (single fixed per-record seed 320; subject to multi-percentage-point variation across independent seed streams); with three genome-derived references its combined pass rate was 0.00% after rounding, whereas GC-target attained 22.68% in each derived condition. A separate v3.3.0 dynamic-programming (DP) execution maximizing the codon adaptation index (CAI) within the same GC window found a GC-compliant sequence for 99.83% of records (49,173/49,257; 84 NO_FEASIBLE_CDS; mean feasible CAI 0.9989), but 28.21% passed all criteria because Type IIS sites are outside the 1DP objective. An independent FactorForge v3.6.4 2x2 factorial evaluation (N = 49,257) crossing codon reference (legacy C1 vs. high-confidence NbeV1.1 C4) and target GC window (55-65% vs. 40-47%) indicates that reference-policy misalignment substantially contributes to the observed zero-pass outcomes, while residual generator limitations remain: switching only the target band to 40-47% under NbeV1.1 increases Assembly-friendly combined pass from 0.00% to 9.39% (11.10% GC-window pass; 81.40% Type IIS-clean) and 1DP to 31.82% (99.998% GC-feasible; mean feasible CAI 0.9412), whereas pairing the legacy reference with 40-47% drops Assembly-friendly to 0.37%. These in-silico results characterize candidate generation on public inputs (UNVERIFIED_PUBLIC_CORPUS); prospective comparison against external tools and laboratory validation remain pending (Biological validation: NOT_AVAILABLE).
